title: Budgeting, Forecasting and Billing: Operational Controls & Revenue Guidance
author: Morgan Patel
content:
Overview
This page documents Redwood Inference’s baseline controls for annual budgeting, rolling forecasting, procurement approvals, contract routing, and revenue recognition/billing practices. The objective is to provide a single operational reference for finance, product, and GTM teams so that budget decisions, vendor commitments, and customer billing are consistent, auditable, and aligned with ASC 606 principles.

Scope
- Applies to all corporate (G&A), product, engineering and S&M spend at Redwood Inference.
- Covers: annual budget process, month/quarter rolling forecasts, procurement approval thresholds, contract review triggers, billing cadence and rev‑rec treatment for common revenue types.
- Does NOT replace legal advice for extraordinary agreements (e.g., M&A, equity/convertible instruments, multi-year government contracts).

Summary of Key Owner Responsibilities
- Finance (FP&A): overall owner of budgeting and forecasting calendar, consolidation, and reporting to execs.
- Procurement (Finance ops / Procurement team): purchase order issuance, vendor onboarding, three-way match.
- Legal: contract template maintenance and final legal review for flagged clauses.
- Product & Engineering leaders: submit budget requests and forecast drivers (headcount, cloud, dedicated capacity).
- Sales & Billing: quote generation, invoicing, dispute handling, and revenue scheduling.

Budgeting calendar (annual + refresh)
1. Jan–Feb: Strategic planning with execs; top-down revenue / ARR targets defined.
2. Feb–Mar: Detailed base-budget submissions from functional managers (headcount, run rate infra, committed vendor contracts).
3. Apr: Finance consolidation, executive review, iteration.
4. May 1: Final budget published (effective fiscal year start).
5. Quarterly refresh: rolling reforecast at end of each quarter with variance commentary > 5%.

Required submission artifacts (per cost center)
- Base budget spreadsheet (headcount by role, FTE start dates, OPEX and CAPEX by vendor).
- Three-year run-rate projection for major capital investments (if > $250k).
- Narrative: three bullet risks, two mitigation actions, and top 3 assumptions.

Forecasting methodology
- Use a 12-month rolling forecast updated monthly; highlight material deltas to prior month (> 5% variance for revenue, > 10% for spend line items).
- Revenue forecast: bookings-driven for subscription and committed contracts; usage-driven for metered products.
- Cost forecast: separate fixed vs variable buckets; apply smoothing for lumpy cloud/GPUs using trailing 3-month average unless specific projects justify variance.

Decision thresholds and approval matrix
| Amount (USD) | Approval needed | Notes |
|--------------|-----------------|-------|
| <$5,000 | Team lead | Auto-approval; capture in monthly spend report. |
| $5,000 – $50,000 | Finance manager + Requester manager | ProcureFlow PO recommended; vendor onboarding required if new. |
| $50,000 – $250,000 | Procurement + Finance director | Competitive bid recommended; contract review if service > 12 months. |
| >$250,000 | CFO + Procurement Head + VP Sponsoring Team | Capital approval process: CAPEX form, board notification if strategic. |

Procurement process (operational steps)
1. Create Purchase Request (PR) in ProcureFlow with business justification and budget code.
2. Procurement validates vendor (KYC, tax, sanctions) and assigns vendor ID.
3. Finance confirms available budget or routes to reforecast.
4. Issue Purchase Order (PO) and track goods/services delivery.
5. Invoice received → three-way match (PO, goods receipt, invoice). Exceptions routed to Finance Ops.
6. Payment run: Net 30 terms default; early‑pay discounts recorded in GL as a contra expense to the supplier spend account.

Vendor onboarding checklist
- W‑9/Tax documentation (US vendors) or W‑8/B for non‑US where applicable.
- SOC2/ISO documentation if handling customer data.
- Insurance certificate minimum: $1M general liability; exceptions documented.

Contract & legal review workflow
- Use ContractHub templates for: Master Service Agreement (MSA), Data Processing Addendum (DPA), Statement of Work (SOW), NDA.
- Legal review required when any of the following apply:
  1. Contract value > $25,000 annually, OR
  2. Any data residency/processing obligations (customer data, PII, HIPAA/PCI scope), OR
  3. Unusual indemnity or liability cap language, OR
  4. Exclusive terms, equity consideration, or multi-year commitments exceeding 24 months.

Contract review checklist (first pass)
- Parties and definitions correct.
- Scope and deliverables (SOW) clearly stated and measurable.
- Payment terms and invoicing cadence defined.
- Liability cap present and aligned to approved threshold (default: 2x annual contract value; exceptions escalate).
- IP ownership and licensing: ensure Redwood retains rights required to operate and support the product.
- Data protection: DPA, breach notification timing (<=72 hours), security controls referenced.
- Termination and transition assistance: commercial and data extraction clauses included.

Revenue recognition (high‑level policy)
- Redwood follows ASC 606 (IFRS 15 equivalent): apply the five‑step model. For the most common arrangements we use the following treatments:
  - Subscription (prepaid annual or monthly): recognize ratably over the service period. If invoiced upfront, record cash as deferred revenue and recognize monthly.
  - Monthly subscription billed in arrears: recognize when service period completes.
  - Usage-based billing (metered API / compute): recognize when usage occurs (measured and billed after month close).
  - One-time professional services (SOW): recognize upon completion of performance obligations (milestone or time-and-material if no distinct deliverable).
  - Renewals/Options: recognize incremental consideration only when distinct performance obligations exist; otherwise treat as continuation of original contract.

Billing & invoicing standards
- Customer-facing invoicing cadence:
  - Subscription annual prepay: invoice at contract signing unless customer requests monthly invoicing; standard terms Net 30.
  - Monthly usage or subscription: invoice monthly in arrears.
  - One-time setup/Professional fees: invoice per SOW terms (milestone or upfront deposit).
- Standard payment terms: Net 30 from invoice date.
- Late payment policy: 1.5% interest per month after 30 days; exceptions require VP Sales + Finance approval.
- Dispute window: Customers must notify billing disputes within 45 days; disputed amounts remain under review — undisputed portions remain payable.

Example journal entries (simplified)
- Annual prepaid subscription (invoice $120,000 on Jan 1 for 12 months):
  - Jan 1: Dr Cash $120,000; Cr Deferred Revenue $120,000
  - Jan 31 (monthly recognition): Dr Deferred Revenue $10,000; Cr Revenue $10,000
- Usage invoice recognized at month-end (invoice $8,400):
  - Month-end: Dr Accounts Receivable $8,400; Cr Revenue $8,400
  - Upon payment: Dr Cash $8,400; Cr Accounts Receivable $8,400

Escalation & audit traceability
- Any contract or procurement routed with non-standard terms must include the deviation reason and approver signatures in ContractHub.
- Finance maintains an audit trail: PRs, POs, signed contracts, invoices and payment evidence retained for 7 years (legal minimum + retention policy).
- Internal audit cadence: annual sample review across OPEX, CAPEX and rev‑rec entries; results shared as a post‑mortem with owners and corrective action plans.

Operational templates (links and snippets)
- Budget change request (BCR) template: include line item, original budget, proposed delta, justification, impact on FY run-rate, approvers.
- PO example (ProcureFlow): PO #: PF-2026-000123; Supplier: ExampleCloud; GL Account: 5001-Infra; Amount: $42,500; Delivery Date: 2026-04-10.
- Contract routing tag set: {"contract_type":"MSA","value_band":"50-250k","legal_review":"required","data_scope":"none"} — populate fields in ContractHub when creating the draft.

Operational norms & best practices
- Encourage multi‑vendor sourcing for large categories to maintain negotiating leverage and meet continuity objectives.
- Use standard templates to reduce legal review time; deviations require business justification.
- Track and report committed monthly recurring cost (CMRC) alongside ARR to understand fixed cost base.
- Forecast uplifts for expected price increases in cloud/GPU contracts at least 90 days before renewal.

Ownership, SLAs and contacts
- FP&A (Budget owner): Morgan Patel — finance@redwood.ai — SLA: monthly forecast published within 5 business days after month close.
- Procurement (PO execution): Procurement Ops (procurement@redwood.ai) — SLA: standard PO issuance within 7 business days of approved PR.
- Billing & AR: Revenue Ops (billing@redwood.ai) — SLA: invoices issued within 3 business days after usage close; disputes responded within 10 business days.

Appendix: Glossary and references
- ASC 606 / IFRS 15: Five-step model (identify contract, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price, recognize when obligations fulfilled).
- Systems: ProcureFlow (Procurement), LedgerPro (ERP/General Ledger), ContractHub (Contract repository), BillingEngine (usage aggregation & invoicing).
- Related pages: procurement vendor scoring, billing dispute resolution playbook, SOC2 evidence inventory.

Change log
- 2024-10-01: Initial draft (Morgan Patel).
- 2025-06-12: Added procurement vendor onboarding checklist and updated approval thresholds (Finance Ops).
- 2026-02-15: Clarified billing dispute window and updated SLAs for invoice issuance (reviewers: Sasha Lee, Priya Menon).

If you have requests to add a country-specific tax treatment or a government contract flow, open a Request For Change (RFC) with FP&A and Legal so we can add jurisdictional guidance and templates.
